The argument's decisive gap is between "the agent did not tell every reporter everything" and "some reporter knows more than all the others." Those premises are compatible with every reporter receiving the same partial account. In that case no reporter knows more than another, so no reporter can scoop the rest, and the conclusion fails. Option B states exactly this consistent scenario, and it refutes the conclusion. The argument fails to recognize that B is consistent with its own premises.

Option C is also a real weakness, since knowing more does not guarantee scooping. But the question asks which option the argument overlooks as consistent with its facts. C does not identify the specific possibility that defeats the conclusion, which B does. The submitted answer's independent check also flagged C as failing to identify the flaw.
